name: sceAcmContextDestroy ioctl request 0xc030ab63 -> 0xc028ab63
tells_game: the request's size field goes back to 0x28; the kernel copies 0x28 bytes of a struct whose first 0x28 bytes have the same fields in both versions, so 13.60's extra trailing 8 bytes are never read
prior_art: the 7.61 kernel's /dev/acm table holds only 0xc028ab63, 0xc028ab01 and 0xc028ab00 (kernel image offset 0x5dcb0b); the native 7.61 lib issues exactly those and the 13.60 lib issues the 0xc030 forms; kernel verified at 7.61 only; hardware: Halo PPSA28038 on 7.61 has audio with the unpatched 13.60 libSceAcm, so nothing observed needs these rows

name: scePadSetVibrationMode: accept modes 4 and 5 for an app stamped below SDK 8.00
tells_game: the mode range check takes the SDK 8.00 branch (modes 1 to 5) whatever the app's compiled SDK word says, so a request for mode 4 or 5 is no longer refused with 0x80920001
prior_art: scePadSetVibrationMode takes 1 ADVANCED (the default; motor levels do nothing), 2 COMPATIBLE, 3 COMPATIBLE2, 4 ADVANCED_AND_COMPATIBLE and 5 ADVANCED_AND_COMPATIBLE2 (names from the SDK's pad header). Through 7.61 the lib accepts 1 to 3 and sends 1, 2 or 3 to the kernel; from 8.00 it accepts 4 and 5 for an app whose compiled SDK is 8.00 or newer. The kernel stores the value unchecked, but its pad driver has motor behaviour only for 2 and 3. hardware at 7.61 (Halo PPSA28038, which requests mode 5 once after scePadOpen): mode 5 refused by the lib gives no rumble although every scePadSetVibration returns 0; modes 1, 4 and 5 sent to the kernel give none; modes 2 and 3 give rumble. Mapping 4 to 2 and 5 to 3 keeps the compatible half of each combined mode; the advanced half is not provided

name: scePadSetVibrationMode: send mode 2 or 3 to the kernel in place of 4 or 5
tells_game: modes 1 to 3 reach the kernel unchanged; a request for 4 (advanced and compatible) is sent as 2 (compatible) and 5 (advanced and compatible2) as 3 (compatible2), so the rumble half of the mode works and the advanced half does not
